discovered_patterns.pattern_name: Specialized multi-agent architecture with central analysis aggregator
evidence: "ORION comprises six specialized agents. Five agents collect core contextual signals, and a sixth agent analyzes them to detect abnormal or risky behavior."

"Unlike traditional DLP alerts triggered by predefined policies, data loss indicators are uncovered by ORION’s set of specialized AI agents through continuous observation of how data moves across your environment."
"The Analysis Agent aggregates all collected signals, transforms them into data loss indicators, and detects deviations from expected behavior."
discovered_patterns.description: ORION implements a multi-agent system: five input/collection agents (Data Classification, Data Lineage, Identity, Environment, External Relations) feed contextual signals into a central Analysis Agent which synthesizes indicators and drives enforcement. Agents appear task-specialized (content classification, lineage tracing, identity enrichment, environment signals, external relationship verification) and are orchestrated to produce intent-aware signals rather than raw policy triggers.
discovered_patterns.why_notable: Applying a compact, purpose-built agent ensemble to telemetry-driven DLP is a pragmatic mapping of multi-agent AI to security: task specialization reduces ambiguity in each signal source and the Analysis Agent functions like a reasoning layer to infer intent, enabling richer correlations than single-model pipelines.

discovered_patterns.why_notable: Lineage + identity + contractual relations (BAAs) fused into real-time DLP decisioning is a strong enterprise-first approach. Integrating contractual constraints (from CRM) into enforcement context is less common in basic DLP products.

discovered_patterns.why_notable: Promptable custom classification embedded in the product enables faster customer-specific labeling without heavy engineering; however, absence of explicit RAG/vector remarks suggests classification may be model-driven on the content payload rather than retrieval from an indexed knowledge base.

unique_findings: Agentized, per-trace telemetry pipeline: ORION describes six specialized agents (classification, lineage, identity, environment, external relations, analysis) that continuously observe every data trace and fuse signals. This is more orchestration-heavy than typical DLP architectures that rely on discrete detectors or single monolithic engines.

Content + provenance + contractual context fusion: Beyond standard content classification, they explicitly ingest CRM/contract data (BAAs, permitted-sharing levels) to decide whether a destination is legitimate. Folding contract-level rules into real-time decisions is uncommon and technically challenging.

Proprietary LLMs targeted at DLP reasoning: They claim to develop proprietary LLMs and ‘specialized AI agents’ to translate low-level signals into data loss indicators (i.e., intent judgments). Using LLMs to operationalize intent detection — not just content classification — is a notable departure from rule/ML hybrids in legacy DLP.

Identity attribute enrichment at scale: The Identity Agent pulls HR/IDP attributes like title, tenure, seniority and even potential departure status to contextualize risk. Using workforce lifecycle signals (e.g., departure risk) in live prevention pipelines is an unusual and high-signal integration.

Slow-drip exfiltration detection as a first-class use case: They call out detection of low-volume, temporally distributed exfiltration patterns. Doing this robustly requires cross-day aggregation, per-user baselines, and graph/time-series correlation across many sinks — not typical for policy-DLP.

Automated indicator discovery + analyst-in-the-loop enrichment: ORION emphasizes learning indicators dynamically and allowing analyst enrichment. This implies closed-loop labeling, feedback collection, and continual model updates rather than static policy tuning.

Policy engine retained but de-emphasized: Instead of discarding policies, they keep deterministic policies for compliance but route ambiguous or contextual cases to the indicator system. This hybrid model recognizes regulatory needs while shifting enforcement to AI reasoning.

competitors.name: Wiz (adjacent / DSPM)
competitors.similarity: Security visibility for cloud risk and data posture; customers often require pairing DSPM visibility with preventive controls to reduce data exposure.
competitors.how_different: Wiz is primarily DSPM/visibility; ORION positions itself as the prevention layer (autonomous DLP) and explicitly markets integration/combination with Wiz to deliver end-to-end protection — ORION claims the prevention capability that DSPM vendors generally lack.

differentiation.primary: Autonomous, intent-aware DLP that replaces or minimizes reliance on static, manually authored policies by using continuous, contextual 'data loss indicators' derived from multiple specialized AI agents and a proprietary LLM.
differentiation.technical: A multi-agent architecture (Data Classification, Data Lineage, Identity, Environment, External Relations, Analysis) that fuses content classification, lineage mapping, identity/HR attributes, environmental signals and CRM/contract context; a proprietary LLM to reason over these signals and continuously learn indicators of risky intent; automated prevention actions (block/prompt/notify) driven by analysis rather than manual rules.
differentiation.business: Go-to-market focused on enterprise verticals sensitive to data exfiltration (finance, healthcare, technology) with claims of rapid reduction in maintenance overhead and near-zero false positives; partnership/integration strategy (e.g., advertised pairing with Wiz) to combine visibility and prevention; messaging and funding to position as a next-gen alternative to legacy DLP vendors.
differentiation.positioning: Positioned explicitly against policy-first DLP vendors: ‘policy reliance is broken’ — ORION markets itself as the modern solution for AI-driven workflows and SaaS sprawl, emphasizing autonomous, context-driven prevention where legacy tools generate false positives and miss novel exfiltration.

secret_sauce.core_advantage: The combination of specialized, continuously running AI agents that collect orthogonal contextual signals (content sensitivity, lineage, identity, environment, external relations) plus a proprietary LLM/analysis engine that synthesizes those signals into automated data loss indicators and intent-aware prevention actions.
secret_sauce.defensibility: Medium — defensible because of (1) data advantage from real customer telemetry used to tune models and indicators, (2) integration breadth (IDP/HR/CRM/lineage connectors) and the engineering required to map cross-system data movement and derive reliable indicators, and (3) a proprietary LLM and agent orchestration that encode domain reasoning. However large incumbents (Microsoft, Broadcom, major CASB vendors) can replicate elements by combining telemetry, ML, and integration at scale, and open LLM technology lowers barrier to entry.
evidence: ORION claims six specialized agents (Data Classification, Data Lineage, Identity, Environment, External Relation, Analysis) that together enable intent-aware detection.
Company statement: 'replaces policies with real-time contextual data loss prevention' and 'automated data-loss indicator analysis' rather than thousands of human-authored policies.
Funding and backing: raised $32M Series A led by Norwest with participation from IBM and others, and claims customers with tens of thousands of employees across finance, healthcare, and technology.
Product claims: near-zero false-positive rate, autonomous blocking/prompting/notification based on indicators, and development focus on proprietary LLM and specialized agents.

competitive_analysis.moat_explanation: ORION’s moat is built on three tangible elements: specialized multi-agent architecture that fuses diverse contextual signals, proprietary LLM and reasoning tailored to DLP, and customer telemetry/connector coverage that improves indicators over time. These create operational value (lower maintenance, fewer false positives) that can win enterprise customers. However, the moat is not unassailable: major incumbents and cloud platform vendors already control many enterprise data planes and large-scale telemetry, have deep customer relationships, and can integrate ML/LLMs into existing DLP/CASB/UEBA stacks. Replication risk is elevated unless ORION can rapidly grow unique data advantage, exclusive integrations, or novel model IP that is costly for competitors to reproduce.

evidence_quotes: autonomous, AI-powered DLP that replaces policies with real-time contextual data loss prevention
indicators are uncovered by ORION’s set of specialized AI agents

Treating 'Data Loss Indicators' as first-class artifacts: synthesizing multi-dimensional contextual signals (content sensitivity, lineage, identity, environment, external relations) into indicators that represent intent rather than relying on static signatures or rules.

A 5+1 agent split: five dedicated collectors for orthogonal contextual domains and a single analysis agent that synthesizes indicators and decides enforcement — a clear separation of signal collection and reasoning.

Hybrid policy model: retaining a policy engine for deterministic compliance scenarios while routing ambiguous or novel cases to autonomous, indicator-driven analysis (policy augmentation rather than full replacement).

Tight integration of enterprise systems (IDP, HR, CRM, DSPM) as signal sources to ground LLM reasoning in enterprise-specific contracts/BAAs and identity attributes, creating richer context than content-only approaches.

Automated indicator-to-action pipeline: indicators not only detected but mapped to automated enforcement actions (block/prompt/notify) with sensitivity settings, implying deterministic action mappings from probabilistic intent signals.
